title: WarrantArtifact
description: PROPOSED, NOT ADMITTED. A recomputable record of what a logic kernel established over a supplied ground set. It records logic only: it does not assert source authenticity, institutional authority, admission, or an execution decision. A warrant is an input to a runtime decision, never the decision itself. See adr/ADR-013.md and docs/contracts/WARRANT-CONTRACT-v0.1.md. VALIDATION IS TWO-LAYER: this schema is structural only. SEMANTIC RULES SC-WA-001 (ground partition) and SC-WA-002 (hash projections) are declared in docs/contracts/ZTL-OCE-MAPPING-v0.1.json and cannot be expressed here, because they depend on the evaluated marking and on the provenance of a digest's input.

kernel_digest.description: A digest emitted by the logic kernel under a declared canonicalization profile. ZTL v0.1 canonicalises with an RFC 8785 (JCS) float-free subset and digests with SHA-384. OIC records this value and never recomputes it.

claim_id.description: Identifier of the admitted proposition the warrant is about. Binds the warrant to a claim, not to a document.

kernel_profile_id.description: Identifies the kernel semantics AND the disposition/grade vocabulary this artifact was produced under, for example `ztl-v0.1`. Dispositions and grades are NOT portable between kernels. A warrant whose profile differs from the control's declared kernel_profile_id is MISBOUND and cannot ALLOW.

canonicalization_profile_id.description: Identifies how `formula` was canonicalised before hashing, for example `ztl-jcs-float-free-sha384-v0.1`. Two formula hashes are comparable ONLY when both this field and kernel_profile_id match the control's declared values. See docs/contracts/WARRANT-CONTRACT-v0.1.md section 5.

formula.description: The formula as the KERNEL rendered it, not as the caller wrote it. Recorded verbatim for replay; OIC does not parse it.

formula_hash.description: Kernel digest over the KERNEL-RENDERED formula (for example `(p ∨ q)` for caller input `p | q`), produced under canonicalization_profile_id. Never computed over the caller's original string. Compared to the control's bound hash by exact byte equality, and only after both profile identifiers match.

disposition.description: The kernel's primary operational signal, and the only field that may drive an OIC decision. MEASURED semantics for ztl-v0.1 over a 294-case census: EARNED = grounded outright, hereditary, raw T, unverified list may be empty or non-empty and is INFORMATIONAL. REFUTED = false regardless of the marks, hereditary, raw F, unverified informational. ON CREDIT = a T verdict true only while an unverified atom holds; its unverified list is LOAD-BEARING. OPEN = not established; its unverified list is BLOCKING. ON CREDIT was omitted from ZTL dossier v0.1 and added after measurement.

raw_verdict.description: The kernel's internal truth marking. REQUIRED for replay, and INERT: it MUST NOT drive any OIC decision. ZTL returns raw_verdict F together with disposition OPEN (measured: judge("p & q", {p:T, q:Z})). An adapter reading this field instead of disposition converts 'not yet established' into 'established false', violating invariant I-03.

warranty_grade.description: How durable the result is under further verification. hereditary is invariant under every admissible monotone refinement of the same formula and marking; sound never lies about the present marking but may stall; until-verification holds only in the present marking. hereditary implies sound. This is half of the result, not optional metadata.

unverified_ground_ids.description: Formula atoms marked Z, echoed verbatim from the caller's marking. Always surfaced as missing_ground_ids on the runtime decision, including on ALLOW. The MEANING depends on the disposition: informational under EARNED and REFUTED, load-bearing under ON CREDIT, blocking under OPEN. Atom IDENTITY is the caller's responsibility.

dependency_ids.description: Every VERIFIED atom (marked T or F) appearing in the kernel-evaluated formula. Disjoint from unverified_ground_ids by construction. This is a deliberate OVER-APPROXIMATION and minimality is NOT claimed: measured, 38 of 180 census cases with two or more verified grounds have a PAIR whose joint withdrawal moves the disposition although neither member does alone, so a minimised set would let a revocation propagate to nothing and leave a stale warrant usable. SEMANTIC RULE SC-WA-001: exactly the atoms marked T or F, disjoint from unverified_ground_ids, and together with them covering the formula's atom set.

ground_epoch.description: Scoped epoch binding. An unscoped integer was insufficient: two ground sets under different authorities can share a sequence number and would compare equal. The kernel is stateless and has no epoch concept; it echoes an epoch supplied by OIC and can neither originate nor validate one.

scope_id.description: Which ground set this sequence counts within. Epochs are comparable only within the same scope.

sequence.description: Monotone counter within the scope. A tick is the arrival of ground; an anti-tick is ground withdrawn.

authority_id.description: The authority that may advance this scope's sequence. Expiry is scoped, never global.

ground_set_hash.description: Digest of the exact ground set supplied to the kernel. Detects staleness an epoch counter alone would miss.

source_anchor_ids.description: Source anchors for the grounds. Supplied by OIC; the kernel never sees sources.

admission_ids.description: Admission records that made these grounds usable. Logic over unadmitted grounds is not a warrant for anything (I-02).

kernel_commit.description: Immutable commit of the kernel that produced this artifact.

output_hash.description: Digest of the semantic output projection: kernel-rendered formula, disposition, raw_verdict, warranty_grade, and unverified identifiers. EXCLUDES `why`, which is presentational and may change without a profile version bump, and `marking`, which is input and already covered by input_hash.

time_binding.description: Identifies the clock or trusted time evidence against which valid_from and valid_until are evaluated. Required because a validity window with no declared clock is unverifiable: two parties can disagree about whether a warrant had expired and neither can be shown wrong. The kernel has NO clock; time is always OIC-supplied or externally attested.

source.description: oic_system_clock is the weakest and carries no non-repudiation. Recording which was used is what makes the evaluation replayable.

reference.description: Identifier of the clock, timestamp token, or time authority relied on.

attestation_hash.description: Digest of the time attestation where one exists. Null for an unattested system clock, which is a stated weakness rather than a hidden one.

valid_until.description: Explicit scoped expiry. Null means no time-based expiry was declared, which is NOT 'never expires': revocation and epoch change still invalidate. Unrestricted expiry trivialises warranties, so expiry is scoped rather than global.

revocation_references.description: Revocation records that would invalidate this warrant if present and in force.

recomputation_reference.description: How to recompute this warrant deterministically: pinned kernel, input hash, and ground set. Required so a warrant is evidence rather than an assertion.

limitations.description: What this warrant does NOT establish. Required and non-empty on purpose: a warrant with no stated ceiling invites over-reading.

allOf.$comment: MEASURED for ztl-v0.1: EARNED is always hereditary with raw verdict T. Its unverified list may be EMPTY OR NON-EMPTY - 61 of 294 census cases are non-empty - and those atoms are informational, not load-bearing.
MEASURED for ztl-v0.1: ON CREDIT is a T verdict riding at least one unverified atom, and is never hereditary.
MEASURED for ztl-v0.1: OPEN never carries raw verdict T (exhaustive search found no counterexample), and always leaves at least one ground unverified.
MEASURED for ztl-v0.1: REFUTED is always hereditary with raw verdict F. Its unverified list may also be non-empty and is informational.
